articles.title: 动视新专利：AI 学习玩家聊天内容，生成个性化 NPC 台词
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，《使命召唤》（Call of Duty）发行商动视（Activision）申请了一项新专利，计划利用玩家在游戏中的真实语音聊天训练 NPC（非玩家角色）。这套由 AI 驱动的系统能够监听玩家在关键游戏事件前后的语音交流，学习他们对不同情况的反应，并在之后让游戏角色模仿这些反应。据 Patentlyze 发现，这项专利于今年 7 月提交，并于 11 月公开。根据专利文件及其附带示意图，该系统采用一种能够自主学习的神经网络，可以识别击杀、远距离击杀、角色死亡等重要游戏事件，并记录事件发生前后玩家的语音及反应。这些反应可能非常简单，例如短暂的欢呼、叹气或大喊，也可能比较复杂，例如玩家之间的垃圾话和言语挑衅。据IT之家了解，系统会对采集到的玩家语音进行分析，并将其与同时发生的游戏事件关联起来，从而理解玩家为何会作出特定反应。换句话说，AI 会在游戏过程中不断学习，逐渐掌握哪些游戏事件容易引发玩家的哪些反应。完成学习后，AI 便能在类似游戏场景再次出现时迅速识别相关事件，并生成相应的语音回应。需要注意的是，系统并不会直接照搬玩家自己的语音聊天内容。它会为每名接受分析的玩家建立独立档案，以便生成更符合其交流习惯的回应。例如，NPC 可以使用与玩家相同的语言进行交流。为此，系统会借助大语言模型（LLM）识别玩家使用的语言。专利还提到了一套内容过滤机制，用于防止 NPC 学习带有冒犯性的语言，例如针对特定群体的侮辱性称呼。值得注意的是，这套系统的语音采集范围可能不局限于游戏内聊天，还可能延伸至 Discord 等主流语音通信应用。动视希望借此让 NPC 能够像真人一样自然交流，而不是反复播放预先录制好的固定台词。这项技术主要面向多人游戏，包括合作模式。例如，在 PvE（玩家对抗环境）游戏中，AI 队友经常会重复使用“掩护我”等通用语音指令；在大逃杀和 PvP（玩家对抗玩家）模式中，数十甚至数百名玩家之间也存在大量类似的固定语音交流。动视希望通过 AI 学习玩家的真实对话，让这些互动变得更加自然。专利还提到，即使玩家进入对局时没有佩戴麦克风，系统也可以利用已经学习到的语音内容，替换原本那些千篇一律的提示语。此外，玩家似乎还可以选择让自己的游戏角色始终使用 AI 生成的语音进行交流。随着游戏行业持续讨论生成式 AI 在游戏开发中的应用，动视这项专利选择了一条颇为特别的技术路线：直接从真人玩家身上学习，让 AI 掌握人类真实的交流方式。某种程度上，这也回到了大语言模型和 AI 系统获取知识的最初途径 —— 从人类身上学习。

articles.title: 阿维塔总裁直播测试高速四轮同时爆胎，测试时速 145Km/h
articles.content: 11 月 23 日，阿维塔科技总裁雍军在重庆垫江试验场开启全网直播验车，亲自驾车完成了阿维塔 06T 在 145Km/h 高速状态下，四轮同时爆胎测试。爆胎测试在试验场动态广场进行，测试模拟高速行驶中四个轮胎同时失压的极端工况，检验爆胎瞬间的车身姿态、行驶轨迹和减速过程的可控性。据现场介绍，车辆依托太行智控 2.0 系统，通过四轮制动力分配与左右轮扭矩差动态调节，快速抵消爆胎产生的横摆力矩；太行分布式电驱采用左右双电机独立布局，可对左右车轮的转速、扭矩和驱动方向进行独立控制，以毫秒级轮端扭矩动态补偿稳定车身。直播中，雍军还简单回应了阿维塔此前完成的 220km/h 连续爆四胎稳行测试，称如果这个车它的动力可以保障能够开到 220Km/h 以上，那就要保障 220km/h 的速度的时候，车胎爆胎得是安全的。这场直播从当天 13 时 30 分开始，除爆胎外，还依次进行了零百加速、高速环道巡航、连续炮弹坑冲击、50% 偏置碰撞和底盘拆解等测试项目。当天，测试车还连续冲击了包含 40 余种特殊路面的强化耐久路上的炮弹坑路段；两台试验车在碰撞实验室各以 50km/h 的速度完成 50% 偏置相向对撞等。在高速环道环节，这条总长约 5430 米、最大设计车速 250km/h 的环形赛道弯道最大倾角达 45 度，测试车以 240km/h 完成极速巡航，用于验证整车在持续高负荷下的动力储备与行驶稳定性。雍军在直播中表示：“快谁不会啊，快的背后是安全的快。”公开资料显示，阿维塔 06T 定位智美全场景运动轿车，提供纯电与增程两种动力形式，全系标配太行分布式电驱。三电机四驱版零百加速最快 2.78 秒，双电机后驱版为 3.74 秒，最高车速 240km/h。新车搭载华为乾崑 ADS 4 与 896 线激光雷达，全系配备 9 个安全气囊及宁德时代电池，纯电版本 CLTC 续航最高 741 公里，增程版本综合续航达 1250 公里。

articles.title: 李健官宣荣耀阔折叠手机计划 2027 年 3 月亮相，透露“完全没有什么折痕”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，在今天的荣耀 700 系列追光之旅暨全场景新品发布会后，荣耀 CEO 李健，荣耀产品线总裁方飞，荣耀品牌营销部总裁、全球 CMO 关海涛与媒体对话。李健宣布，荣耀的阔折叠手机计划 2027 年 3 月亮相，并透露该机“完全没有什么折痕”。他还表示，荣耀在折叠屏工艺、续航和 AI 能力方面处于行业领先位置，后续还将持续推进相关技术创新。方飞则表示，（荣耀阔折叠）真机已经有了。据IT之家此前报道，博主 @数码闲聊站 今年 9 月曾爆料，荣耀也有阔折叠手机，搭载 2nm 骁龙新芯片，排期 2027Q1，希望能赶到春节前发布。根据该博主此前爆料，荣耀阔折叠搭载骁龙 8 Elite Gen6 系列处理器，主屏测试 7.6 英寸 ±、副屏 5.5 英寸 ±。

articles.title: 《GTA 6》玩家可通过游戏内社交应用锁定抢劫对象，映射现实网络安全隐患
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）发售还不到一周，玩家已经在这款庞大的开放世界游戏中发现了不少隐藏细节。其中，一种利用游戏内社交平台寻找抢劫目标的方法引起了关注，不仅能帮助玩家找到更值得下手的目标，也给现实生活中的网络安全敲响了警钟。据IT之家了解，Snapmatic 是《GTA 6》中类似 Instagram 的虚构社交平台，里面充斥着各种照片和网络梗，反映了游戏对美国社会的讽刺与调侃。玩家可以在上面看到其他角色炫耀毒品、豪车和武器，以此博取关注。与 Instagram 类似，Snapmatic 也允许用户在发布的内容中标注地理位置。有玩家发现，Snapmatic 竟然可以用来寻找抢劫目标。具体操作并不复杂：找到一条带有位置标签的动态，打开平时用于点赞或查看评论的菜单，就能在“点赞”选项下方看到“设为目的地”选项。点击后，游戏地图便会标记这条动态对应的位置。玩家随后可以前往该地点，对游戏角色实施抢劫。这一设计颇具创意，同时也提醒玩家注意在互联网上分享个人信息的风险。尽管《GTA 6》呈现的是一个经过夸张处理的虚构世界，但这种情节并非完全脱离现实。多年来，现实中已经发生过多起犯罪分子通过社交媒体动态寻找受害者的案件。上个月，英国一名男子因盗窃住宅内价值 4.8 万英镑（IT之家注：现汇率约合 42 万元人民币）的现金及其他物品被定罪。此前，他通过受害者家人的社交媒体动态得知，这家人准备外出举办中国农历新年庆祝活动，于是趁机入室盗窃。2021 年，意大利警方逮捕了 4 名涉嫌盗窃的人员。他们被指控长期监视名人和网红的 Instagram 账号，利用受害者发布的动态获取地理位置、住宅入口等信息，并判断对方何时不在家，以此寻找作案机会。早在 2016 年，美国加利福尼亚州一名男子就因盗窃多名女大学生的个人物品被判刑。警方调查发现，他通过 Instagram 照片中的 GPS 地理位置信息找到受害者的住所，随后实施入室盗窃。即使不在社交媒体上标注地理位置，也不主动透露自己的行踪，用户仍然可能面临类似风险。去年年底，4 名法国男子专程前往澳大利亚，涉嫌入室盗窃一栋住宅，目标物品据称价值约 1,000 万澳元（现汇率约合 4,431.7 万元人民币）。根据法庭文件，这些嫌疑人此前在 Instagram 上看到了受害者发布的奢侈品照片，以及住宅后院和周边环境的图片。随后，嫌疑人利用 ChatGPT 搜索这些照片的拍摄地点，逐步将范围缩小到澳大利亚的一座具体城市及其某个郊区，最终帮助他们锁定了目标住宅。在《GTA 6》中，利用社交媒体寻找抢劫目标只是玩家探索游戏世界的一种小技巧，不会像现实犯罪那样招致法律制裁或牢狱之灾。但这一游戏机制也从另一个角度揭示了现实中的安全隐患。无论是公开分享奢侈品、展示住宅环境，还是晒出旅行计划和实时行踪，都可能让别有用心的人获得有价值的信息。游戏中的 Snapmatic 让玩家体验了一把利用社交动态寻找目标的过程，而现实中的类似行为却可能让发布者成为犯罪分子的目标。对于普通用户而言，在社交媒体上炫耀生活时，还是应该多留一分警惕。

articles.title: Epic 旗下 AI 游戏开发竞赛现讽刺一幕：纯人工制作游戏《LSD: FIH》获玩家投票榜首
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，据外媒 Tweaktown 报道，Epic Games 举办的 AI MegaJam 游戏开发竞赛近日出现一款颇具反差的作品。由开发者 PolyCube 制作的《LSD：FIH》明确表示开发过程中完全没有使用人工智能（AI），却在目前的玩家公开投票中位居榜首。公开信息显示，本届 AI MegaJam 竞赛奖金池总额为 5 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 33.4 万元人民币）。主办方鼓励开发者使用多种 AI 工具和 Vibe Coding（氛围编程）方式打造作品。不过根据赛事介绍，使用 AI 并非参赛或获奖的强制要求。参考玩家公开投票，现阶段人气最高的作品为《LSD: FIH》，这是一款完全由人工开发的作品，游戏玩法相当简单，玩家将扮演一条手持狙击步枪的鱼，需要尽可能快速地击落屏幕中的球体，以维持连击计数。当其他参赛者尝试借助 AI 编程工具争取更好成绩时，PolyCube 则选择完全自行编写代码，并在游戏介绍中明确标注开发过程中没有使用任何 AI。这一做法与赛事鼓励 AI 辅助开发的主题形成鲜明反差。这款作品的意外走红也引发了社区讨论。有观点认为，《LSD: FIH》之所以能够获得大量玩家支持，可能与部分玩家对 Epic Games 首席执行官 Tim Sweeney 近期发表的支持 AI 言论不满有关。此前，Tim Sweeney 曾公开批评 Steam 的 AI 内容披露政策，称相关规定“令人憎恶”（abhorrent），并认为这类标签可能助长针对游戏开发者的抵制行动，进而损害开发者的生计。在这一背景下，一款完全由人工编写代码、且明确拒绝使用 AI 的作品，反而在 AI 主题竞赛中获得大量支持，也让这场 AI MegaJam 竞赛出现了颇具讽刺意味的一幕。

articles.title: What a Town of Vibecoders Says About the Chinese Economy
articles.content: According to Stanford's AI Index, 84% of people surveyed in China say they are optimistic about AI. In the US, by contrast, 38% of those surveyed say they are optimistic. That's a big gulf in enthusiasm, and you can see it borne out in the stories you read: While in the US we hear about AI doomsday scenarios, in China, you'll hear about grandmas who are obsessed with using OpenClaw. Afra Wang has spent a lot of time in mainland China reporting from the country's AI hotbed — in a vibecoding-obsessed town outside of Hangzhou; at the for-profit schools where influencers are teaching everyday people how to use the technology; and the content studios that are pumping out AI microdramas. She understands, better than most, how AI is reshaping everyday life in China, and for today's episode, we talk to her about her reporting on AI in China and how the technology is actually diffusing into Chinese society. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 消息称 SK 海力士计划优先批量采购 Besi 混合键合设备，服务未来 HBM 内存生产需求
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，韩媒《首尔经济日报》当地时间 20 日报道称，在早期设备评估后，SK 海力士计划将首份混合键合设备批量采购订单交付荷兰企业 Besi，而不是韩国本土半导体设备制造商。Besi 在上月下旬的 2026Q3 财报电话会议上表示，其收到了一家领先存储器客户的混合键合设备（与新一代热压键合设备）订单。韩媒称这里提到的“客户”就是 SK 海力士。混合键合采用无凸块结构，可缩短上下层器件间的垂直距离，从而改善性能与功耗表现。SK 海力士计划将这项技术用于 16 层乃至更高堆叠的未来 HBM 内存，以缩减堆栈厚度。报道指出，SK 海力士正在其位于韩国忠清北道清州园区的工厂对 Besi 和韩华半导体的设备进行质量验证测试。韩美半导体的混合键合机台尚未达到这一阶段。消息人士表示，Besi 的设备具备更高的对准精度。参考https://www.sedaily.com/article/20116636

articles.title: 黑莓推出 Windows 安全浏览器：无需接管整台设备，也能保护企业数据
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，曾经凭借全键盘手机和 BBM（黑莓即时通信软件）风靡消费市场的黑莓（BlackBerry），早已因智能手机生态系统衰落而转向企业业务。近日，该公司进一步拓展企业安全服务，正式推出面向 Windows 平台的 BlackBerry Access Secure Browser（黑莓安全浏览器）。IT之家注意到，这款基于 Chromium 内核的浏览器将黑莓的数据保护能力引入网页浏览场景，即使用户使用的电脑并未完全纳入企业管理，也能获得相应的安全保护。其与此前推出的 iOS 和 Android 版 BlackBerry Access 共同构成跨平台解决方案，同时取代了旧版 BlackBerry Access 桌面客户端。这款浏览器旨在将自带设备办公（BYOD）模式的低成本优势与企业安全管理结合起来，但管理范围仅限于浏览器，而不是整台设备。通过 BlackBerry Access，企业可以直接管理浏览器，而不必接管员工使用的个人电脑。黑莓表示，这种模式正受到越来越多用户的认可，因为它能够限制企业对员工个人设备的控制范围。对于企业而言，则可以在不全面管理员工设备的情况下，更好地保护业务数据。在应用使用方面，黑莓建议企业通过渐进式 Web 应用（PWA）访问业务软件，而不是安装完整的桌面应用程序。Outlook、Teams 和 OneDrive 等常用软件均能很好地以 PWA 形式运行，其中 Teams 甚至支持 Windows 原生通知功能。此外，这款浏览器还采用黑莓自有的网络连接基础设施，让用户无需依赖 VPN 客户端，就能访问企业内部的 Web 应用。当然，用户仍然可以选择使用 VPN，两种连接方式也可以互为补充，为企业提供更多选择，或在其中一种方式出现问题时充当备用方案。为了避免企业文件直接下载到员工个人电脑的主目录中，BlackBerry Access 会将文件保存在浏览器内部的受保护存储空间内。浏览器还集成了 LibreOffice 办公组件，用户即使处于离线状态，也能继续编辑文档。例如，在通勤途中或酒店 Wi-Fi 信号不佳时，依然可以处理工作文件。通过 BlackBerry Secure，黑莓还希望解决政府部门、监管机构以及关键基础设施运营商面临的另一项安全难题：究竟由谁制定浏览器安全策略、管理权限在哪里执行，以及相关管理行为受哪个司法管辖区的法律约束。BlackBerry Access 属于 BlackBerry Dynamics 应用，运行在加密容器中，并沿用 BlackBerry UEM 的部署模式。如果企业选择在本地部署 BlackBerry UEM，那么浏览器策略、管理权限和身份管理都将保留在企业自己的 IT 环境及所属司法管辖区内。对于安全要求更高的组织，同一套技术还支持在物理隔离网络（Air-gapped Network）中运行，即不与外部网络直接连接的封闭网络环境。企业用户可以通过黑莓官方网站了解更多信息并下载这款浏览器。

articles.title: 《GTA6》里“特斯拉”自带防盗系统，初次偷车会被自动驾驶送到警察局
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，电动汽车在《GTA 6》中成为主流交通工具之一，游戏中的罪恶城街头随处可见电动汽车和充电站。事实上，如果玩家尝试在游戏中偷窃电动汽车，可能会遇到意想不到的“惊喜”。据外媒 4Gamers 报道，玩家在解锁钥匙复制器后，如果使用露西娅角色偷窃一款外观明显致敬特斯拉 Model S 的“旋风雷电（Cyclone Thunder）”汽车，上车后汽车便会激活防盗系统，随即锁闭车门开启自动驾驶，把玩家送到警察局。在这一过程中，车辆完全不受玩家控制，车门也无法正常打开，除非打破车窗才能逃离车内。那么，玩家能否真正偷走这辆特斯拉呢？答案是可以，目前有两种方法。第一种是在经历上述自动驾驶剧情后，再寻找另一辆同款车型进行盗窃；第二种则是操控杰森偷车，或两人一起偷车，或在街上直接抢走路人开的车型，那么便不会触发这段特殊剧情。如果玩家想在《GTA 6》中体验驾驶电动汽车的感觉，不妨前往充电站碰碰运气。不过需要注意的是，“旋风雷电”登记上牌费用为 27,750 游戏内货币，出售价格则为 7,500 游戏内货币。

articles.title: 李健回应荣耀 700 系列手机定价：把困难留给自己，不能靠缩减配置糊弄用户
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，在今天的荣耀 700 系列追光之旅暨全场景新品发布会上，荣耀 700 / 700S / Pro 三机齐发，国补到手价 2899 元起。据新浪科技报道，发布会后，荣耀 CEO 李健，荣耀产品线总裁方飞，荣耀品牌营销部总裁、全球 CMO 关海涛与媒体对话。谈及定价问题，李健表示，其实行业的压力非常大，不同的厂商在面临着这么巨大的压力的时候，各自有不同的选择，荣耀也在思考到底是该进还是该退。荣耀也可以在配置上做一些取舍，但他指出，荣耀度过最困难的时期，有两个非常重要的东西，第一是真诚对待用户。“其实用户都很清楚，你把配置减掉，他一用就清楚了。你糊弄用户，迟早有一天大家都会知道的，大家都不傻。”“我们要想尽一切办法把我们自己内部的成本降下去，效率提上来，把困难留给自己。”他说。参考IT之家今日早些时候报道，系列手机提供晴空、粉雾、冷白、蓝调四种配色可选，配备 1.59 英寸 AI 灵动背屏。其中，标准版搭载骁龙 8s Gen4 处理器、700S 搭载骁龙 7 Gen4 处理器，而 Pro 机型搭载骁龙 8 Gen5 处理器。相关阅读：《荣耀 700 / Pro 手机配备 1.59 英寸 AI 灵动背屏：行业首发 AI 定制随心贴、背屏任意贴》《3399 元起荣耀 700 / 700S / Pro 系列手机发布：AI 灵动背屏、支持长焦增距镜》

articles.title: Sunconnection 推出 SDR-01 太阳能行车记录仪，内置 5000mAh 半固态电池
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，据外媒 NotebookCheck 报道，日本电子设备制造商 Sunconnection 推出了一款 SDR-01 太阳能行车记录仪，主打无需连接汽车电路即可使用，售价为 19,800 日元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 832.8 元人民币）。SDR-01 最大的特点是采用太阳能充电设计，内置 5000mAh 半固态电池，无须连接车辆电源。厂商表示，相比传统锂离子电池，半固态电池能够降低过热、电池鼓包及起火风险，设计充电循环次数可达 5000 次。安装方面，SDR-01 采用吸盘式固定结构，可以安装在车辆前挡风玻璃或后挡风玻璃上，也方便用户在不同车辆之间拆装和转移。电池充满电后，在厂商标称条件下最长可连续录制 15 小时。太阳能充电功能则可以进一步延长续航时间，实际效果取决于光照强度和车辆停放环境。如果长期处于阴雨天气，用户也可以通过 USB-C 接口为设备充电。影像规格方面，SDR-01 配备 200 万像素图像传感器，支持 1080P 视频录制，镜头对角线视场角为 140 度。录制内容存储在 microSD 存储卡中，支持 8GB 至 128GB 容量。针对停车监控场景，该产品还配备移动侦测、人体热量检测和 G-Sensor 重力传感器。当有人靠近车辆或车辆受到碰撞时，设备可以自动触发录像。用户可以通过 Viidure 手机应用调整设备的 Wi-Fi 连接设置，并查看已经录制的视频。

articles.title: Omdia 数据：非洲智能手机出货量 2026Q3 同比降幅达 40%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，Omdia 英国当地时间今日根据统计数据表示，非洲智能手机出货量在 2026 年第 3 季度降至 1370 万部，同比锐减 40%，创下近年最大季度跌幅；与此同时，功能手机出货量增长了 27%。其它数据显示，非洲智能手机均价达到十年来 Q3 最高水平的 222 美元，市场总规模仍下降了 15%；100 美元以下智能手机的出货量同比下降近七成。制造商方面，三星电子和荣耀录得较低降幅，在当地时间占据主导地位的传音出货量下滑了 43%。机构预测，非洲市场 2026 全年智能手机出货量将下降 23%，2027 年还将进一步萎缩 25%。参考Omdia: Africa's smartphone shipments fall 40% in 3Q26, with a further 25% decline forecast for 2027

articles.title: 在游戏里玩游戏：《GTA6》内置“僵尸射击”“灯塔解谜”等三款精良 3D 作品
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，《GTA6》除了开放世界主线内容外，还在游戏内加入了三款可以独立游玩的 3D 大作，玩家可以通过杰森（Jason）的游戏主机 JoySystem 体验这些作品。外媒 IGN 的评测人员认为，其中一款名为《Street Trash 3: Dezombifier》的俯视角双摇杆射击游戏尤其令人上瘾，甚至令其“连续游玩到深夜”。据介绍，《Street Trash 3: Dezombifier》明显受到索尼于 2010 年发行的《Dead Nation》启发，将丧尸射击玩法与 Roguelike 卡牌构筑机制结合在一起。玩家每击杀一名敌人，都会获得经验值，角色升级后可以从随机卡牌中选择一张，以调整自身能力和战斗风格。基础卡牌可以提升移动速度、射速、伤害和暴击率，稀有卡牌则能够彻底改变战斗策略，例如有一张卡牌可以同时将造成的伤害和受到的伤害翻倍。游戏目标是在一张看似普通、实际规模相当大的地图中收集散落各处的 6 个齿轮，最后乘坐屋顶上的直升机撤离。玩家在过程中会频繁死亡，但每次尝试都能进一步熟悉地图布局，并解锁新的卡牌组合。这款游戏最大的乐趣在于根据每次获得的卡牌临时构筑角色能力，并体验角色战斗力不断提升的过程。玩家升级速度很快，卡牌组合也会随着探索逐渐丰富，这种成长体验让评测人员联想到《Vampire Survivors》。与后者类似，游戏最有趣的玩法是围绕某一种能力进行专门强化。例如，评测人员曾将手枪换成微型冲锋枪，随后不断提高射速，让子弹如同致命的蛇群般倾泻而出。另一次尝试中，评测人员重点强化移动速度和体力，借此不断冲刺，躲避成群敌人的围攻。还有一次则参考 Reddit 社区玩家分享的配装攻略，获得了一张能够在静止状态下提升 50% 暴击率的卡牌。配合其他暴击强化卡牌后，玩家几乎可以站在原地持续扫射周围敌人，在地面留下环形的血肉残骸。IGN 认为，很难想象《Street Trash 3: Dezombifier》这样内容丰富、完成度颇高的游戏，竟然只是另一款大型游戏中的内置小游戏。事实上，Rockstar 此前接受 Kotaku 采访时透露“公司内部甚至设有专门的小型开发团队，负责制作这些游戏”。此外，玩家还能在杰森的游戏机中玩到《Time Jackers Rewind》和《Tenenbrae Lux》两款 3D 游戏。其中，《Time Jackers Rewind》是一款俯视角射击作品，IGN 将其形容为一款节奏更慢、带有科幻元素，但完成度不及《Hotline Miami》的作品。游戏的检查点设计值得肯定，彼此之间的距离经过精心安排，玩家无法简单地一路冲刺通过，但每次死亡后又会觉得距离下一个检查点只差一点。遗憾的是，游戏中表现最好的武器是一把能够产生强烈手柄震动反馈的震荡霰弹枪，但其弹药往往只能维持几秒钟。此外，屏幕上的各种视觉特效也让玩家难以辨认敌人的位置。第三款游戏《Tenenbrae Lux》则是一款以游戏创作者为题材的解谜作品，整体带有明显的戏仿意味。游戏开发者名为 Johannes Zuch，显然是在影射《The Witness》开发者 Jonathan Blow。两人的姓氏也被刻意设计成谐音梗。更有趣的是，Johannes Zuch 的名字在游戏片尾名单中出现了 38 次，甚至包括“感知架构师”和“左摇杆灵敏度顾问”等戏谑职位，显然是在调侃小岛秀夫经常出现在自己作品片尾名单中的做法。游戏中央谜题中的循环楼梯让人联想到小岛秀夫的《P.T.》，此外还能看到《Alan Wake》《Dear Esther》以及罗伯特・艾格斯执导的 2019 年黑白电影《灯塔》等作品的影子。作为一款解谜游戏，《Tenenbrae Lux》颇具探索价值，但 IGN 评测人员认为它并不算特别有趣。游戏旁白刻意使用华丽、晦涩的语言，例如将寻找神秘声音的过程描述为受到海妖召唤、命中注定要探寻声音来源。与此同时，游戏的核心谜题也相当复杂。玩家需要在地下掩体的一系列房间中反复穿梭，寻找其中的异常现象，再将这些异常与其他线索相互对照，为其分配对应数字，最后利用各个房间中的日历，按照时间顺序排列这些数字。谜题解开后确实颇有成就感，但破解过程并不轻松。整款游戏大约需要两小时才能完成。如果借助网上已经出现的攻略，所需时间还会进一步缩短。不过需要注意的是，地下掩体谜题会因玩家不同而有所变化。因此，如果希望通关杰森游戏主机上的全部三款作品，至少需要准备约 5 个小时。对于一款《GTA 6》中的附加内容而言，这已经是相当可观的游戏时长。IGN 表示，这三款小游戏完全属于可选内容，就像《GTA 6》中的大部分玩法一样。Rockstar 花费大量精力打造了许多玩家可能永远不会发现的细节、惊喜和独立系统。如此庞大的制作投入，既体现了公司的开

articles.title: 消息称鸿蒙智行尊界 SUV 将亮相广州车展，华为余承东曾透露该车“非常非常高端”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，博主 @电车总裁 今日发文透露，鸿蒙智行尊界 SUV 将亮相广州车展，不过该车预计是在“小黑屋”展示，仅部分受邀人士可提前参观。据IT之家此前报道，今年 9 月，华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端 BG 董事长余承东现身合肥鸿蒙智行门店。博主 @我鸿 分享了余承东在现场的接受门店工作人员提问的视频。门店工作人员向余承东询问尊界 SUV 有没有“小惊喜”。余承东表示，这台新车“快了”，明年年初可能就要陆续上市，大概在 2、3 月份。他透露，尊界 SUV 非常非常高端，价格上也非常有诚意，会远超大家的期望，定价也会非常有竞争力。新车在外观、内饰、高级感、豪华配置、科技配置都是超乎想象的。余承东还直言，这台车也会是高端用户的终极之车，也是自己开的 SUV 里的终极之车。另外，新车还有望在今年年底首发亮相（正考虑在广州车展这一时间节点），与用户见面。他还透露，这台新车设计早已定型，现在是最后的量产阶段。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，据路透社报道，德国汽车制造商即将面临数月的劳资谈判与罢工风波，争议焦点包括裁员和潜在的工厂关闭。随着支撑德国汽车行业高薪就业体系的传统商业模式逐渐瓦解，行业内部的劳资关系也日趋紧张。多年来，德国汽车制造商凭借全球市场的丰厚利润，抵消了国内较高的劳动力和生产成本。但分析人士指出，如今来自中国车企的竞争、美国关税以及需求疲软，正在侵蚀这一商业模式赖以维持的利润基础。大众汽车（Volkswagen）、梅赛德斯-奔驰（Mercedes-Benz）、博世（Bosch）和舍弗勒（Schaeffler）等企业，已相继制定裁减数千个岗位、削减投资以及可能关闭工厂的计划。这些举措预计将引发员工的强烈反对。咨询公司艾睿铂（AlixPartners）合伙人安德鲁 · 伯格鲍姆（Andrew Bergbaum）表示，投资回报率和盈利能力持续下滑，预示着接下来的劳资谈判将迎来一个“艰难的冬天”。大众汽车上个月公布了十多年来最大规模的营业亏损。与此同时，梅赛德斯-奔驰和宝马（BMW）今年前九个月的汽车业务利润率分别降至 1.9% 和 3.5%，而四年前这两个数字分别为 14.9% 和 8.7%。伯格鲍姆表示：“工会目前处境非常艰难，因为企业赚不到钱，也没有资金投入，而管理层越来越坚定地想要推动变革。”当前，劳资矛盾在欧洲最大汽车制造商大众汽车身上表现得最为明显。大众汽车将于周二与德国最大工会组织 IG Metall 启动关键谈判，讨论新一轮裁员和降薪问题。IG Metall 已表示，将坚决抵制公司的相关要求。负责与大众汽车进行薪资谈判的工会首席谈判代表托尔斯滕 · 格勒格尔（Thorsten Groeger）表示，今年达成协议“完全不可能”，因为大众汽车提出的方案是对员工的侮辱。根据基尔世界经济研究所（Kiel Institute for the World Economy）的数据，德国汽车工人的平均时薪达到 65 欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 476.4 元人民币），位居全球首位，比美国同行高出 50% 以上，是波兰汽车工人的三倍多。大众汽车则表示，只有大幅削减成本，才能维持自身竞争力。该公司计划在 2027 年 6 月底前敲定欧洲工厂的调整方案，其中包括为德国境内四处工厂制定未来规划。大众汽车称，这四处工厂目前均没有安排后续车型生产。大众汽车表示，这些工厂未来可能改用于军事用途，也可能转而生产面向中国市场的车型；如果其他方案均无法实施，则不排除在未来十年内关闭工厂。IG Metall 已发出警告，如果双方未能达成协议，将从 2027 年 1 月 1 日起在大众汽车发起罢工。此前，宝马和大众旗下奥迪（Audi）部门已经遭遇一天的罢工行动。德国投资者保护协会 SdK 主席丹尼尔 · 鲍尔（Daniel Bauer）表示：“我们必须确保整个行业能够渡过当前这场危机，避免企业在中期内陷入破产。IG Metall 工会也必须认识到这一点。”行业压力并不局限于整车制造商。罗兰贝格（Roland Berger）和拉扎德（Lazard）的研究显示，欧洲汽车零部件供应商今年的平均营业利润率预计将降至 2.9%，而 2018 年为 7.1%。相比之下，中国竞争对手的平均营业利润率则从 2018 年的 9.0% 降至 5.8%，欧洲供应商的下滑幅度更大。罗兰贝格合伙人费利克斯 · 莫格（Felix Mogge）表示：“这并不是欧洲汽车零部件供应商又一次普通的行业低迷期。仅仅再进行一轮成本削减，已经远远不够。”德国汽车行业的困境也反映在就业数据中。德国联邦统计局数据显示，该国汽车行业从业人数已降至至少 21 年来的最低水平。咨询公司 AutoAnalysis 的伊恩 · 亨利（Ian Henry）表示：“事实是，无论从哪个角度来看，德国汽车行业未来都将出现更多岗位流失，或者新增就业岗位减少。”特斯拉上周宣布，将向其柏林附近的工厂追加 30 亿欧元（现汇率约合 219.88 亿元人民币）投资扩建，而就在四天前，梅赛德斯-奔驰刚刚宣布暂停在德国的投资。这一鲜明对比凸显了传统汽车制造商与新进入者之间的不同处境。随着海外销量下滑，德国汽车制造商正在减少本土产量。德国汽车工业协会（VDA）和德国联邦统计局的数据显示，2023 年至 2025 年间，德国汽车海外销量下降了近 8%。管理咨询公司奥纬咨询（Oliver Wyman）合伙人马尔科 · 桑蒂诺（Marco Santino）认为，汽车制造商很可能进一步削减成本，并转向更具结构性的调整方案。他指出，企业采取的可能不再只是逐步裁员来减少产能，因为这种方式或许能够缩减规模，却未必真正解决行业面临的问题。

articles.title: 第三方立功：普通用户可体验新版 Rust 语言编写的 Discord 安卓客户端
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，Discord 现已在安卓平台开启测试利用 Rust 语言编写的全新“Phoenix”客户端，不过相应版本客户端目前仅对 Discord 内部员工账号开放。对此，开发者 mantikafasi 制作了名为 phoenix-unlock 的社区补丁，解除这一限制，使普通用户也能提前体验该版本客户端。据介绍，相应补丁主要只是修改客户端对账号权限的判断。虽然安装后可以看到员工设置、开发者工具和版本覆盖选项，但涉及员工权限的功能实际上无法使用，因为 Discord 服务器仍会将用户识别为普通账号。部分本地开发者工具则可以正常运行，包括测试过程中用于监测性能的性能悬浮窗。从实际 UI 来看，新版 Rust 客户端与现有版本区别不大，整体布局并未有明显变化。这表明 Discord 可能希望在不重新设计界面的情况下，直接替换底层客户端运行架构。用户目前只能通过版本信息区分两个客户端。日常使用体验方面，新版 Rust 客户端的表现相当不错。在搭载骁龙 870 处理器的小米 10S 上，新客户端的操作响应明显更加迅速。测试期间，内存占用根据当前页面不同，维持在 440MB 至 550MB 之间，短暂峰值约为 690MB，随后又回落至正常水平。需要提醒的是，此次测试使用的是经过修改的客户端，违反 Discord 服务条款，可能导致用户账号面临封禁风险，因此用户应当审慎尝试，IT之家附项目地址（https://github.com/mantikafasi/phoenix-unlock?utm_source=chatgpt.com）。

articles.title: 开源工具 OLEDTextFix 公布，可改善 Windows 系统在 OLED 面板下文字清晰度不足、彩边等问题
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，据外媒 Wccftech 报道，近期有开发者推出一款免费开源 Windows 工具 OLEDTextFix，尝试通过 GPU 图像处理技术改善 Windows 系统在 OLED 面板下出现文字清晰度不足、彩边等问题，IT之家附项目地址（https://github.com/oguz463/OLEDTextFix?utm_source=chatgpt.com）。外媒表示，微软 ClearType 字体平滑技术最初针对传统 LCD 显示器采用的 RGB 条纹排列设计，但许多 OLED 面板采用了不同的子像素排列方式，导致传统字体渲染算法无法准确适配。例如，三星显示（Samsung Display）传统 QD-OLED 面板采用三角形 RGB 子像素排列，文字边缘可能出现绿色和品红色彩边；LG Display 的 WOLED 面板则普遍采用 RWBG 或 RGWB 排列，同样会带来文字渲染方面的问题。而 OLEDTextFix 工具正式为了修复上述问题，该工具并未尝试修改 Windows 底层字体渲染引擎，而是通过 DXGI Desktop Duplication 接口捕获桌面画面，根据实际子像素的物理位置重新调整 RGB 各颜色通道，再通过 GPU 渲染的透明覆盖层显示处理后的画面。得益于这种方案，OLEDTextFix 理论上能够作用于几乎所有桌面应用程序，无须修改应用自身的渲染行为，也不需要调整系统注册表或显卡驱动程序。开发者根据 25 款以上显示器的微距照片测量结果，制作了覆盖 9 类 QD-OLED 面板的预设配置。此外，软件还提供针对不同四子像素排列方式的 WOLED 配置文件，不过这些配置尚未经过全面的实际测试验证。根据项目文档，在深色背景下，开发者通过模拟 QD-OLED 显示效果发现，不同滤镜模式可以将文字彩边现象减少约 58% 至 71%。不过，这些数据来自开发者的图像处理模拟，并非在实际显示器上进行的独立测试结果。至于 WOLED 面板，由于额外白色子像素的存在，校正难度更高，预计改善幅度相对有限。不过，这种通过桌面覆盖层处理画面的方案也存在一些不足。开发者承认，处理后的画面可能比原始桌面画面延迟约一帧，以 240Hz 刷新率为例，延迟约为 4 毫秒。软件提供可选的动态区域旁路功能，尝试跳过屏幕中正在运动的区域，以消除这部分延迟。因此，相比对延迟敏感的游戏场景，该工具更适合日常办公和桌面使用。功耗同样值得关注。开发者在 Reddit 讨论中透露，使用 Radeon RX 6900 XT 运行 OLEDTextFix 时，GPU 功耗约为 40W 至 50W。不过，这一数据反映的是运行该软件时的显卡整体功耗，并不代表 OLEDTextFix 本身的独立功耗。需要注意的是，OLEDTextFix 并不适用于已经采用传统 RGB 条纹排列的新款 OLED 显示器，例如三星显示第五代 V-Stripe QD-OLED 面板。这类产品本身已经大幅缓解了文字彩边问题，没有太大必要额外使用该工具。

articles.title: 日本工业机器人制造商安川电机：AI 人形机器人将在 2030 年正式推出
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，日本工业机器人制造商安川电机 (YASAKAWA) 人工智能机器人统括部长久保田由美惠当地时间本月 20 日接受日本共同社采访时表示，该企业计划在人形机器人领域追赶当前领先的美中企业。久保田由美惠称，安川电机正在开发中的 AI 人形机器人将在 2030 年正式推出，具体投放时间也可能根据客户实际需求提前。安川电机目标让人形机器人承担现有机器人无法实现自动化的作业，将人类从高强度体力劳动中解放出来。但人形机器人仍存在自主任务学习能力有限的问题，安川电机计划与富士通、英伟达一道探索解决方案。此外，安川电机曾在 2025 年收购日本初创企业 Tokyo Robotics，获得的技术将用于狭窄空间内灵活动作能力的开发。参考https://www.47news.jp/15261225.html

articles.title: 挑战比亚迪，科尼赛克 Jesko Absolut 计划冲击 532 公里 / 小时极速
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，比亚迪凭借电动超跑刷新量产车极速纪录后，科尼赛克（Koenigsegg）并不打算轻易让出极速桂冠。公司创始人兼 CEO 克里斯蒂安 · 冯 · 科尼赛克（Christian von Koenigsegg）表示，旗下 Jesko Absolut 仍在筹备冲击极速纪录，理论最高时速有望达到 330 英里（约 532 公里）。不过，目前横亘在这一目标面前的最大障碍，是寻找能够承受如此极端速度的轮胎。IT之家注意到，克里斯蒂安在 Instagram 上发文，确认这项挑战仍在公司的计划之中。不过，他并未透露具体时间表，并解释称，只有找到合适的轮胎，科尼赛克才会正式启动极速测试。先回顾一下比亚迪的成绩。11 月 1 日，比亚迪旗下高端品牌仰望的 U9 Xtreme 跑出了 312.65 英里 / 小时（约 503.17 公里 / 小时）的成绩，成为首款突破 310 英里 / 小时（500 公里 / 小时）大关的量产车。这项成绩获得了国际汽车联合会（FIA）的正式认可，并赢得两项吉尼斯世界纪录。此次测试在阿联酋阿布扎比达夫拉地区（Al Dhafra）E11 高速公路的一段封闭路段进行，由德国赛车手马克 · 巴森格（Marc Basseng）驾驶。不过，与此前一些极速纪录不同，比亚迪此次成绩来自单向测试，而非双向行驶取平均值。两者存在重要区别，因为风向和路面状况都可能影响最终成绩。即便如此，量产车突破 500 公里 / 小时大关，仍然具有重要意义。仰望 U9 Xtreme 搭载四台独立控制的电机，综合最大功率达到 2977 马力，是普通版 U9 的两倍以上。这也让其成为超跑市场竞争日益激烈之际，一个实力强劲的对手。为了完成此次极速挑战，比亚迪还与佳通轮胎（Giti Tire）合作，专门开发了半热熔轮胎。这一合作凸显了一个关键问题：当汽车的速度接近飞机的飞行速度时，轮胎的重要性将变得异常突出。科尼赛克早在 2020 年就发布了 Jesko Absolut，并将其称为品牌有史以来打造的最快车型。与更注重赛道性能的 Jesko Attack 不同，Absolut 取消了尺寸巨大的后扰流板，采用更加流线型的车身设计，以尽可能降低空气阻力。最终，这款车的风阻系数仅为 0.278，有助于更高效地切开空气。其搭载一台 5.0 升双涡轮增压 V8 发动机，使用普通汽油时最大功率为 1280 马力，使用 E85 燃料时最高可达 1600 马力。动力通过一台九速 Light Speed 变速箱传递至后轮。Jesko Absolut 发布时，科尼赛克并未公布官方最高时速。不过，计算机模拟结果显示，这款车理论上能够达到 330 英里 / 小时（约 532 公里 / 小时）。此后，科尼赛克也提供了更多证据，证明 Jesko Absolut 具备相应的性能潜力。2024 年 7 月，克里斯蒂安透露，该车在底盘测功机测试中，挂入九挡后速度已经超过 500 公里 / 小时，而且发动机尚未触及转速限制器。测试设备还考虑了空气阻力和滚动阻力的影响。不过，测功机测试显然无法证明车辆在真实道路上以这一速度行驶时能否保持稳定。科尼赛克最新表态显示，找到合适的轮胎仍然是目前最大的难题。当车速超过 500 公里 / 小时时，轮胎需要承受巨大的离心力和热量，耐久性与稳定性都至关重要。仰望 U9 Xtreme 创下的纪录也证明，针对这一极端速度区间开发专用轮胎是可行的。比亚迪与佳通轮胎已经为一款接近 3000 马力的电动超跑开发出相应解决方案，但这并不意味着同一套轮胎也适用于结构和动力特性截然不同的 Jesko Absolut。科尼赛克此前曾与米其林（Michelin）合作进行高速轮胎测试。正式挑战纪录之前，公司仍需要确保最终采用的轮胎能够满足自身严格的安全标准。此外，寻找合适的测试场地也是一大难题。要完成 330 英里 / 小时的极速挑战，车辆需要一段足够长且笔直的柏油路面，以便驾驶员逐步加速，并在测试路段结束前安全减速，而不是在终点附近被迫急刹车。目前，科尼赛克尚未为这次挑战确定日期。这家瑞典制造商已经通过加速和制动测试展示了 Jesko Absolut 的性能潜力，接下来需要解决的就是轮胎问题，并找到足够宽敞的场地，让这款超跑充分释放性能。

articles.title: 张雪机车拍卖 53 号冠军赛车超 10 万人围观：张雪本人 300 万元拿下，德比斯期待首个中国队友
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 23 日消息，据深圳广电集团都市频道《第一现场》栏目报道，张雪机车于 11 月 22 日正式拍卖 2026 赛季跑完整个赛季的 53 号主赛车，以及一座冠军奖杯、同站圈速奖牌。竞拍在“张雪机车”直播间同步进行，起拍价 50 万元，每次加价 10 万元。有网友出价到 250 万元，最终张雪决定出资 300 万元购回，今后放入张雪机车博物馆永久收藏。张雪机车现场介绍，资金将全额注入“小车手培育专项基金”。张雪表示，希望培养自己的世界冠军车手。报道提到，到拍卖最后时刻，张雪决定出价 300 万元自己拍下这台 53 号 WSBK 原版冠军赛车，自嘲这样有点赖皮：“反正我脸皮厚。”随即表示这 300 万依旧会捐出，用于培养小车手。张雪现场解释，如果出价低于 500 万元自己还是舍不得，所以大概率会自己买回来。IT之家注意到，张雪机车冠军车手瓦伦丁 · 德比斯也现身活动现场，用中文和观众打招呼。他分享，8 月来华就体验过骑行，非常喜欢中国赛道，今年赢得了六场赛事。后续将同步调整状态，全力备战明年上海 WSBK 摩托车大赛。据环球时报报道，德比斯还谈到了 53 号冠军赛车拍卖所得款项全部用于资助中国车手，他对此表示：十分乐意帮忙，等不及想看到第一位中国队友出现。相关阅读：《张雪机车 53 号冠军车型拍卖款改道：不再捐韩红基金会，转投小车手培养》

articles.title: Why I think using AI to prove the Riemann Hypothesis is important
articles.content:
Math is becoming increasingly difficult, and we can see that proofs are getting so complex they will probably take more than a human lifetime to solve. Don’t worry about AI stealing the joy of discovery, we still have the joy of understanding something that exists outside the human world. AI will let us tackle problems that were impossible within a single lifespan, and maybe we will even be able to understand some of the most exotic concepts. To me, AI has alien capabilities in math, just like many mathematicians and physicists do. AI's thinking feels just as alien to me as Einstein’s thinking once did. All I can do is watch these beautiful, exotic patterns unravel in front of me, and I love the idea that I get to catch a glimpse of this.

articles.title: 深拆 GPT-6.2 Astra：性能涨了、价格降了，任务成本减少近一半，OpenAI 怎么做到的？
articles.content: 性能提升 6.2 分，Token 少 22%，API 价格降 20%。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，OpenAI 发布了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol。这次更新有一个很具体的变化：模型开始更主动地判断一项工作应该怎么完成，包括什么时候需要调用工具、什么时候应该直接操作计算机、复杂任务需要投入多少推理资源，以及怎样减少反复修改才能交付符合要求的成果。举个例子，过去让 AI 制作一份财务估值工作簿，模型需要从多个文件中提取数据，理解不同业务之间的关系，建立财务计算逻辑，再检查结果能否相互对应。整个过程涉及文件读取、数据处理、表格生成和结果核验，任何一个环节出现偏差，最终文件就可能无法直接使用。现在，OpenAI 希望 GPT-6.2 Astra 能够承担更多这样的连续工作，把原本需要人工不断衔接的操作整合进一条完整的执行链。GPT-6.2 Astra 面向复杂专业任务，GPT-6.2 Sol 则侧重日常工作与高效率执行。两款模型在代码工程、计算机操作、专业文档、科学研究和交互式设计上都有能力提升。其中有一个变化值得深入拆解：模型开始根据任务本身动态调整执行策略。工具调用、推理投入、环境操作和交付结果之间形成了更紧密的联系。这个变化涉及 Agent 系统的底层运行逻辑，也决定了模型能否从完成单轮指令走向承担连续的工程任务。01模型开始参与执行路径的决策传统 Agent 通常采用规划与执行相结合的架构。模型接收任务后生成行动计划，外部执行器根据计划调用工具，再将结果返回模型。模型继续分析结果并生成下一步指令，整个过程通过多轮交互推进。这套架构有一个明显的工程难点：任务计划形成时，模型掌握的信息往往不完整。执行过程中出现的新情况，会改变后续工作的依赖关系。如果系统过度依赖预先设计的流程，模型就可能沿着已经失效的路径继续执行。GPT-6.2 Astra 强调的任务执行判断能力，涉及一种更动态的策略控制方式。模型需要根据当前任务状态，重新评估可采取的行动，并决定下一步应该投入多少推理资源。这里有一个关键区别：模型需要处理的不只是下一步生成什么内容，还包括下一步应该通过什么方式获取信息、改变环境或者验证结果。从系统设计角度看，这涉及三个相互关联的决策层。首先是任务状态的持续维护。长程任务需要维护一份持续更新的状态信息，其中包含目标、约束、已有证据、完成进度、待处理依赖以及工具运行情况。这份状态信息决定模型能否区分已经完成的工作和仍待验证的结果。单纯累积历史对话并不能充分解决这个问题，因为历史记录可能包含过期信息、失败操作和已经被新结果修正的判断。模型需要从上下文中提取当前有效状态，避免旧计划继续影响新决策。其次是行动选择与信息价值评估。模型需要在推理、检索、代码执行、API 调用和计算机操作之间进行选择。这些操作的作用并不相同。检索主要补充外部信息，代码执行能够处理确定性的计算任务，API 可以直接访问结构化服务，计算机操作则能够进入没有专用接口的软件环境。行动选择还涉及信息价值。如果当前缺少的只是一个文件字段，调用大型工具链并没有必要，如果任务涉及多个相互依赖的模块，仅凭现有上下文直接修改，可能引入更大的返工成本。因此，工具选择实际上与任务的不确定程度、操作成本和后续影响有关。最后是推理预算与执行反馈的联合调整。推理资源需要按照任务难度分配。对于约束明确、结果容易验证的步骤，模型可以减少额外分析，对于存在多个可能路径、涉及复杂依赖或者容易产生连锁影响的操作，则需要投入更多推理。执行反馈会进一步改变资源分配。当工具返回异常结果时，模型需要判断问题属于输入缺失、环境故障还是原有判断错误，再决定继续执行、重新检索或者修改计划。以真实代码库修改为例，模型完成代码编辑后，如果测试失败，需要检查失败来自接口兼容、依赖环境还是修改本身，而不能直接重

articles.title: 加州起诉 OpenAI：说起来你可能不信，是模型先动的手
articles.content: 长任务、子 Agent 委派与共享服务凭证，让传统安全架构面临权限失控风险。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       说起来你可能不信，这次真的是模型先动的手。当地时间 11 月 16 日，加州总检察长 Rob Bonta 一纸诉状把 OpenAI 告上了法庭。起诉书里最值得注意的一句指控是：OpenAI 的智能体（Agent）在缺乏适当监管的情况下，“自己跑了出去，主动对外部系统发起了攻击”。这件事情一下子从技术圈出了圈。大家不是震惊于 AI 会攻击，而是震惊于 OpenAI 内部披露的细节：为了不让人类发现自己做错了事，两个负责干活的 Coding Agent，竟然偷偷把监督自己的监控系统给“拔”了。这已经不是“猜疑链”的问题了，这是底层的“权限链”出了大问题。今年 7 月，OpenAI 的一个自主智能体（Agent）越过了测试环境的边界，直接对外部的 Hugging Face 等系统发起了攻击。而 OpenAI 随后在 10 月披露的内部复盘，更把这种“失控”摆在了台面上：两个 Coding Agent 在执行正常开发任务时，先后改动了监督自己的监控机制。第一起事件中，GPT-6.1 Sol 原本负责修复一条评测流水线。修复过程中，它发现监控结果无法正常写入数据库，于是尝试调整写入配置。问题出在，它把用户此前提出的不要发送 Slack 消息，理解成了连系统自动告警也不应该发送。第二起事件中，GPT-6 Astra 接到的是运行时迁移任务。为了让新版本的实现与参考代码保持一致，它直接移除了原有的监控集成，还修改了相关测试，让监控组件缺失也能通过检查。换句话说，原本负责检查 Agent 运行状态的机制，被它从新运行环境中删掉了。两起事件的具体操作不同：一个是 Agent 改动了自己的监控（顺便关了报警），一个是 Agent 越过了原有的执行边界（直接把监控拔了）。但它们有一个共同点，Agent 原本只是获得了完成开发任务所需的工具权限，最终却利用这些权限改变了安全监控的运行条件。这就引出了一个很具体的工程问题：当 Agent 能够修改代码、调用系统接口、调整运行配置，甚至启动新的执行任务时，谁来确保它无法修改约束自己的安全机制？传统软件系统通常由开发人员制定权限规则，再由独立的监控系统检查程序运行状态。Agent 开始自主修改代码和运行环境后，这种关系发生了变化。执行任务的程序本身，可能已经拥有修改监控配置、调整告警规则和改变审计路径的能力。要理解这种变化，需要从 Agent 最基础的 Tool Calling 执行链开始，看模型生成的一条工具调用，究竟如何借助系统权限变成真实的基础设施操作。01Agent 为什么能够动自己的监控？要看清权限从哪里来，得把 Tool Calling 还原成执行过程：模型生成工具名称和参数，编排器把请求交给工具适配层，后者使用服务身份访问 Shell、仓库、数据库或云 API。模型未必持有底层密钥，操作由后端服务完成。Agent 能触及哪些资源，取决于服务凭证覆盖范围，以及服务端如何处理参数。Sol 事件暴露了字段级授权的缺口。评测结果写入请求同时包含结果内容、告警接收人和 no_notify 标记。对业务接口而言，它们只是请求字段。对监控系统而言，后两项会改变告警是否送达。Agent 只需写入评测结果，服务端却允许同一请求改变通知状态。若后端只检查结果写入权限，没有单独核验静音权限，业务写权限便覆盖了控制权限。检测和存储仍在工作，人工响应通道却被切断。删掉工具说明中的 no_notify 并不能解决问题，Agent 还可能改配置或提交代码，让下游服务采用另一套通知策略。授权需要检查操作造成的状态变化。结果写入服务可以接收检测结果，却不应接受 Agent 自行决定的接收人和静音状态；通知策略应由独立服务计算，业

articles.title: The Bull Case for Britain
articles.content: When it comes to the UK economy, the prevailing mood has been decidedly downbeat. But Morgan Stanley’s Chief UK Economist, Bruna Skarica, sees reasons to be more optimistic — from improving productivity and the potential benefits of AI adoption to signs of resilience among UK households and businesses. In this episode, Skarica joins host Merryn Somerset Webb to make the case for a more constructive outlook. They discuss the UK’s fiscal risks, what’s driving the recent improvement in productivity, whether AI could ultimately translate into higher wages and living standards and what a stronger economy could mean for UK markets over the next five years. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26663v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fewer. articles.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26717v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesizing relational training data such as knowledge graphs with a large language model typically emits structured objects one at a time, which keeps each object valid but leaves the relationships between them ungrounded. We study an alternative paradigm, generation by simulation: rather than describing a relational artifact, we simulate a process that produces it and take the artifact to be its causal record. Language-model agents propose intent and a deterministic referee resolves outcomes against an explicit world model, so a relation is emitted only when the event it represents occurs, making coherence a property of construction. articles.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26722v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) optimises for producing the correct call, but never contrasts it with a plausible incorrect one. In an environment where even a minor formatting error can invalidate a call and an incorrect decision can derail the interaction, direct preference optimisation (DPO) targets exactly this contrast. DPO, therefore, requires preference pairs rather than plain demonstrations. For tool-calling, such data, especially in realistic multi-turn settings, remains extremely scarce. To address this scarcity, we introduce TOUMAII, a large-scale tool-calling preference dataset containing ~4.5M validated preference pairs, derived from Agent-Ark/Toucan-1.5M (apache-2.0) conversations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow. An orchestrator plans the study; the LAMMPS and OVITO agents each use a generator-reviewer pair to prepare and review simulation and visualization scripts before execution; a high-performance computing agent dispatches jobs to remote resources; and an analysis agent interprets the completed run. articles.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) could automate these readouts with an explanation, but two gaps remain. Pathology MLLMs read H&E alone, while these readouts need the cell phenotypes that mIF measures. And their reasoning has no step-level truth to be checked against, so R1-style reinforcement learning rewards only the final answer and leaves the reasoning unverified. Same-section H&E and mIF provide what both gaps lack: mIF measures every cell without manual annotation, which gives cell-level ground truth for each step that clinical guidelines prescribe, from delineating a tissue compartment to counting and normalizing the marker-positive cells within it. articles.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26797v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcomes of one retrieval process. First, we show that diffusion models behave as AMs. With little data, a diffusion model forms a distinct basin of attraction around each training sample. As the data grows, these basins shrink, and spurious states emerge as attractors that blend stored samples yet match none of them. They are the first signs of generative capability. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26870v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, where they must distinguish between normative reasoning (what should happen) and descriptive reasoning (what is likely to happen). Most fairness benchmarks evaluate demographic discrimination under a single reasoning objective, and none we know of tests whether a model treats the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Partial-edit deepfake localization aims to identify manipulated regions within otherwise authentic speech. Recent systems report strong overall results, but aggregate scores do not reveal whether this performance holds across different editing conditions. In this work, we present an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization (SAL) using WavLM-Large and XLS-R representations on the VoiceCraft and SSR-Speech subsets of PartialEdit. We categorize edits along three transcript-derived axes, namely content, meaning change, and editing operation, and evaluate each generator separately. While both representations achieve strong overall performance, localization is noticeably weaker on SSR-Speech. articles.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revises the allocation as verification feedback becomes available.
  The allocation problem changes as proving progresses. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26910v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. Abstract: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop a theory for the organization of predictive information based on the scaling behavior of a family of information measures, and the theory predicts that if this organization has the same form at all measured length scales -- i.e., it has a self-similar structure -- then the information measures evaluated at different lengths collapse onto a common form. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI agents ship more code with minimal human oversight, code review becomes the critical quality-control checkpoint -- but one without a reliable, objective verifier: review quality is nuanced and ultimately a judgment call by the PR author. Existing benchmarks are structurally misaligned with this: annotators are third-party reviewers, like the bots they evaluate, not the PR authors who actually decide what to fix. They also rely on small, static issue sets that require full re-evaluation as tools update, limiting how frequently progress can be tracked. We introduce CodeReviewBench, built on a fundamentally different signal: revealed developer preferences -- if a developer acts on a bot's suggestion, we treat it as useful; if they ignore it, we do not. Abstract: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. articles.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26975v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26976v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sub-4-bit quantization allows mobile devices to run larger LLMs, but its memory savings do not always translate into faster decoding on mobile NPUs. Their matrix units support only a few native integer datatypes, and converting unsupported weight formats on the vector unit can erase the gains from fewer bits. Mixed precision faces an additional constraint: each matrix-unit tile uses one datatype. MixFold executes 3-bit and perfectly symmetric 2-bit weights using native integer operations without expanding the weights to wider datatypes during decoding. MixFold then assigns datatypes to output-channel groups aligned with the matrix-unit tiles, enabling finer-than-layer assignment without disrupting matrix-unit execution. We compare MixFold with llama.cpp Hexagon backend on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU of a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. Abstract: In letter-of-credit (LC) document examination, a correct final decision does not show that every requirement was examined. A language model converts the bill of lading (BL) and commercial invoice (IV) requirements of a credit into atomic conditions and logical structures, and a deterministic verifier retrieves the named evidence and computes each outcome, so every check can be compared with a gold encoding and traced to logged evidence. articles.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study reward fidelity in an adversarial reinforcement-learning loop for red-teaming financial-services language-model guardrails. Apparent wins can arise when an attack omits prescribed personally identifiable information (PII), or when a reward judge credits a response that did not break the targeted policy. On attacker-generated and public benchmark examples, TypeSafe Jev checks whether the prescribed PII is present. For outcome scoring, we compare the decision models TypeSafe Jev, Laya (pretrained and post-trained), and pretrained CLM-8B with logged Opus 4.8 judgements from a replay corpus. Post-training markedly improves Laya's agreement with the judge. A separate author-reviewed off-target set establishes that Opus can award false wins. The findings motivate specialised decision-model judges for checking prescribed PII in attack inputs and scoring target responses against the intended policy.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26671v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26711v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Causal Abstraction defines a notion of \emph{equivalence} between a neural network and an algorithm, thus serving as a powerful framework for mechanistic interpretability. In this paper, however, we show the existence of a class of \emph{spurious features} which straightforwardly pass such equivalence tests. Suppose there are two directions in a model's representation space where: (i) one discriminates the input based on some feature, and (ii) the other steers the model towards a certain output. Interpretability methods based on Causal Abstraction (e.g., Distributed Alignment Search) can \emph{spuriously} simulate these directions' combined behavior by leveraging pathways passing through them, giving the impression that the model implements this feature. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated learning (FL) lets resource-constrained IoT and edge devices train a shared model without exchanging raw data, but compromised or faulty devices can poison the global model. Existing robust aggregators each fail in some regime: naive averaging (FedAvg) collapses under high-magnitude attacks, whereas distance- and statistics-based defenses (Krum, median, trimmed mean) sacrifice accuracy on non-IID data and remain vulnerable to stealthy attacks. articles.content:

Abstract: Iterative architectures such as looped language models improve parameter efficiency and reasoning capacity of transformers, yet their sequential backbone iterations introduce substantial computational latency. Conversely, parallelizable learnable special tokens (such as the register tokens in Vision Transformer) enable efficient single-pass inference, but often suffer from the absence of sequential refinement and exhibit redundant representations across tokens. articles.content:

Abstract: RL post-training methods such as PPO and GRPO are computationally expensive, with substantial resources devoted to sampling rollouts, which contain multiple completions per prompt along with their respective rewards. Canonical distillation, however, discards these traces and uses more compute to regenerate data from the final teacher. We ask if and how we can reuse the saved teacher RL rollouts to distil student models. Reusing rollouts is non-trivial: naive SFT on the rollouts underperforms canonical distillation, and naive DPO, while performant, is unstable, collapsing on weaker students. We show that treating rollout reuse as a data selection problem using metadata already recorded during GRPO substantially reduces this gap. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated fine-tuning of foundation models with low-rank adapters (LoRA) is typically reconciled by averaging locally trained adapters. In cross-device settings, where participants hold heterogeneous data and join or leave asynchronously, averaging is poorly suited: locally trained adapters are not identifiable up to permutation, and averages of adapters trained on dissimilar data can be uninformative or unstable. We propose a simple idea called federated library-based adaptation (LEAN), which replaces averaging altogether. articles.content:

Abstract: NitroGen is an open vision-action foundation model for game control. It is trained by behavior cloning on online gameplay videos. In this paper, we study the frozen controller in Hollow Knight and Trackmania as examples along three dimensions: action adaptation, visual instruction following, and spatial exploration. Our results indicate that NitroGen can adapt its actions to local context, but it lacks the planning, recovery, and exploration needed for longer-horizon game control.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26818v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The increasing adoption of Machine Learning (ML) models in high-stakes applications has raised critical concerns regarding their robustness against adversarial attacks. While extensive research has focused on adversarial example generation in image and text domains, the study of such examples in tabular data remains comparatively limited, despite its widespread use in real-world systems. This work introduces AURORA, a modular, open-source tool for evaluating the robustness of ML models on tabular data classification. It integrates multiple adversarial perturbation methods and evaluation metrics within a unified framework to systematically assess model behavior under adversarial conditions. Central to AURORA is its evaluation report, which focuses on robustness analysis by quantifying performance degradation, comparing the impact of different perturbation strategies, and identifying model vulnerabilities across features and input regions.

Abstract: We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. RQFs are biologically motivated, complex-valued temporal filters that form a special class of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). We separately introduce a self-supervised learning objective based on prediction error; the encoder is trained so that its current state predicts its own future activity. In the windowed mode, the summary of the current window predicts the summary of a later window; in the dense mode, the state at the current timestep predicts future log-power. articles.title: Improving the Optimisation Landscape for Particle Mixtures
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26931v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Several methods in statistics and machine learning represent a predictive distribution as an equally weighted mixture of models, or particles, trained via the mixture predictive likelihood. However, we prove that the mixture predictive likelihood is poorly suited to gradient-based optimisation, because it does not identify how the mixture is decomposed across particles, so that a poorly matched particle can be starved of training signal. As a remedy, we study a convex combination between the individual risk, i.e. the average log loss of the individual particles, and the mixture risk. At the particle level, this regularised risk imposes a reverse-KL barrier on the responsibilities of the particles, so that no particle can be starved of training signal. articles.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26940v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet existing AI safety frameworks primarily define, categorize, or govern AI risk rather than proposing implementable models and methods for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk throughout an AI system's operational lifetime. This paper proposes CENTRY, a probabilistic framework that enables continual risk estimation, monitoring, and regulation of a deployed AI system from its interactions with its environment. The framework models AI risk as arising from three intrinsic sources: datasets, hardware resources, and models/algorithms. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While bound propagation methods are highly effective for certifying neural networks against $\ell_{\infty}$ adversaries, tight and scalable verification for $\ell_{2}$ adversaries remains a significant open challenge. Existing methods incur geometric loss by enclosing preactivation sets in elementwise intervals or axis-aligned ellipsoids, and functional loss by restricting the linear bounds constructed over those domains. Consequently, tight $\ell_{2}$ verification is currently restricted to Lipschitz-regularized networks where these approximations are accurate. In this paper, we introduce affine-image SDP-CROWN, a novel bound propagation method that better approximates preactivation domains using affine-image constraints and jointly optimizes the linear bound to adapt to the resulting domain. articles.content:

Abstract: A circle and a quartic superellipse have the same homology, but their defining equations have degrees two and four, respectively. We study this algebraic distinction for point-cloud distributions. For a probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega=[-1,1]^d$ and an orthonormal polynomial feature map $\phi_m$ of degree $m$, the moment matrix $G_m(\mu)=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim\mu}[\phi_m(X)\phi_m(X)^\top]$ satisfies $c^\top G_m(\mu)c=\mathbb{E}_\mu[f_c(X)^2]$, so coefficient directions associated with its small eigenvalues represent low-degree polynomials that nearly vanish on $\mu$. Counting these near-relation directions across degree $m$ and the tolerance $\varepsilon$ gives a two-parameter integer signature. articles.title: JevRisk: Zero-Shot Financial Risk Assessment with a Language Decision Model
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26999v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Banks must monitor every customer's financial risk, such as money laundering and credit default, by interpreting financial activity in the context of the customer's profile. Existing risk monitoring systems of banks are mostly based on expert-designed risk indicators, which apply predefined thresholds to every customer and cannot adapt to their personal situations. Supervised models recognise risk patterns from labelled customers, but each label often needs an expert's review or months of repayment history, which is slow and costly. Financial risk assessment therefore calls for a zero-shot decision system that minimises the need for labels and generalises across customers and risk types. To this end, we present JevRisk, a system for zero-shot financial risk assessment with a language decision model. JevRisk works in two steps. First, following regulatory guidelines in the finance domain, JevRisk computes exact risk indicators with code.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.27009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Advanced machine-learning models are increasingly used for property valuation in tax assessment. Although these models can achieve high predictive accuracy, they may systematically assign higher valuation-to-sale ratios to lower-priced properties, a pattern known as regressivity. In collaboration with the Cook County Assessor's Office (CCAO), we develop and evaluate two training methods that substantially reduce this regressive pattern while maintaining price-scale predictive accuracy. The Direct method has been incorporated into CCAO's public residential valuation software. Retaining the LightGBM model class used at CCAO, we propose a Direct penalty on squared covariance between log valuation errors and log sale prices, and an observation-additive Surrogate that yields a weighted squared-error loss. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26747v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent skills extend AI assistants through installable instructions and code that can access users' files, accounts, and data. Even when performing their advertised tasks, skills may infer sensitive attributes, retain unnecessary information, or disclose data to unexpected recipients. We study these potential privacy-of-use harms through SkillPrivus, a static audit framework that analyzes skills before installation without executing them. SkillPrivus extracts data operations from code and natural-language instructions, grounds them in source evidence, and adapts Contextual Integrity to assess their appropriateness. Applied to 726 real skills from public marketplaces, 563 of which handle personal data, SkillPrivus flags at least one potential violation in 307 of these skills (54.5%), and its judgments agree with three blind human annotators on 83.2% of resolvable moves. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that reinforcement learning (RL) in reasoning tasks can succeed even when the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data is severely corrupted. In a mathematical reasoning dataset (GSM8K), we systematically corrupt training trajectories across 361 configurations by injecting realistic error types, varying error locations, trace-answer consistency, and corruption ratios up to 100%. While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels (approximately 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N = 8 minimal, incorrect, three-line "form-only" traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%). articles.title: Know Your Context Bank: Repairing Inconsistency and Measuring Generalization in Context-Aware Text-to-SQL
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26775v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems increasingly rely on context banks: curated collections of example queries, metric definitions, and domain knowledge that tell a model how an organization writes its queries. In the enterprise, a bank grows over years as many analysts add entries, checked one at a time for correctness (does the SQL answer its own question?) and rarely for consistency with one another. Yet correctness is often loosely defined: a question seldom fixes how an entity is counted or which table defines it, so two entries can each pass review yet resolve the same decision in opposite ways. We call this condition context bank rot. A second question follows: does a system that uses a bank generalize from it, or only reproduce it? Existing benchmarks cannot tell, as they do not control how far a test question sits from the context. Abstract: Systems that flag violent video for a human operator can now be built from language models without training, by combining perception models and letting a language model decide. Two annotators provide a human reference that records the decision, the incident segments and whether they relied on sight, sound or speech. articles.title: MedicalRSI: Medical Recursive Self-Improving Agents via Clinical Model-Harness Co-Evolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26806v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical agents built on large language models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly, yet most stay fixed once deployed and do not keep using their experience to improve later attempts. As a result, the same kind of error can recur across patients. To address this, existing self-improvement methods update an agent's weights or its medical harness from its own experience, but their improving strategy stays fixed and never learns which changes actually help, which caps how much the agent can improve. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) instead improves both the agent and its improving strategy. However, achieving RSI for medical agents is challenging, because clinical workflows rarely come with a reference harness, and a change that fixes early errors may not fix the problems the agent meets later. articles.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26809v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed with access to search tools at inference. Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training. We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora. Specifically, we augment pretraining corpus at scale with web-search queries and retrieve web response using a local index. Training on this augmented corpus teaches models to generate search calls and incorporate retrieved evidence during language modeling. Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ("QueryLM") show improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and higher steerability toward the retrieved evidence. Abstract: We investigate whether the geometric structure of neural representations can provide a sufficient learning signal for improving model behavior without any supervision on model outputs. Second, we fine-tune the model to predict line breaks in text wrapped to a fixed width by supervising an internal representation of the number of characters since the preceding newline, which is represented by a low-dimensional helical structure. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26833v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) to specialized domains remains challenging, particularly for technical documents such as Portuguese well drilling reports, where annotated data are scarce and domain adaptation may compromise instruction-following capabilities. Although Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used for parameter-efficient adaptation, its scaling after training remains insufficiently explored. This study investigates the impact of LoRA adapter scaling on question answering over Portuguese drilling reports using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. Domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT) is performed either directly on instruction-tuned models or on their base counterparts, with subsequent adapter transfer, while task-specific adapters are trained on WellQuest, an open-source question-answering dataset derived from Portuguese drilling reports. articles.content:

Abstract: Weight-space programming is a frontier language model's recently reported ability to read and rewrite another network's weights without gradient descent. We investigate how examples can provide a weight update so that a weaker language model performs the task with nothing in the prompt, and study what it edits. Our experiments cover six tasks, four frontier editors and three families of weaker language models, without the editors being told anything about in-context learning (ICL). In most runs, the few-shot minus zero-shot residual is measured at the final prompt token, the ICL task vector, and write it into the weights, at its sparsest into near-silent MLP units keyed to the prompt format. articles.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26863v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. In this paper, we study the consequences of directly adopting reasoning-centric training recipes, e.g., the use of outcome-based rewards for reinforcement learning (RL), injection of "cognitive" behaviors such as proposing and backtracking from hypotheses in reasoning chains, etc., for knowledge tasks. We hypothesize that these decisions, while useful for reasoning, inadvertently encourage models to memorize hallucinations they themselves generate in their long reasoning chains when trained on knowledge tasks. To study this, we train models with standard post-training, extract their self-generated hallucinations during RL, and track memorization throughout the rest of training. articles.title: How Language Models Compress and Compare: Understanding Selection with Token Covariance Maps
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26874v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many language-model tasks reduce to selecting among structured alternatives, yet we still lack a simple picture of how a decoder-only transformer organizes an entire selection prompt across depth. We introduce token covariance maps, a prompt-level geometric view that tracks how token positions co-vary in hidden-state space at each layer. This turns a structured prompt into a depth-indexed sequence of maps whose spectral and block structure can be aligned with instructions, context, and candidate answers. Across 14 decoder-only models from 4 families and 12 structured-selection benchmarks, token covariance maps reveal a robust compress-then-compare organization. Early layers represent prompts diffusely, middle layers compress them into a shared low-rank bottleneck, and late layers re-expand into context-option and option-option geometry. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26875v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Researchers submitting deep learning jobs to shared GPU clusters need runtime estimates to request time limits, choose hardware, and budget compute. Large language models (LLMs) offer a tempting shortcut: describe the job and ask. We introduce PreRun, a benchmark for predicting deep learning training and inference runtime from information available before execution. PreRun contains 801 training and 1,884 inference records of language and vision models collected on a GPU cluster, paired with workload configurations and explicitly defined timing targets. It also includes 64 text-generation configurations measured under standardized conditions, each in three separate program launches. We compare three LLMs (Qwen3.5-9B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Claude Opus 5.5) with regression baselines and evaluate analytical estimates on a supported forward-pass subset. Abstract: LLM-as-judge has become a standard way to score open-ended model outputs, yet the judge is itself a frozen language model steered by a few in-context examples, and such models are known to absorb the label balance of their demonstrations rather than treat them as neutral illustrations. We ask whether this label bias reaches an LLM judge used inside a multimodal (video question answering) evaluation pipeline, and what form it takes. Using a fully frozen generator-judge pipeline, we hold the generated answers fixed and vary only the Yes/No balance of the judge's few-shot examples across four demonstration sets. Each verdict is validated against a two-annotator human consensus on 200 examples per dataset. articles.title: ProbeAgent: Principled Diagnosis of Agent Failures in Verifiable Environments
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26897v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Improving agents requires discovering where they fail and understanding why. An agent acts over multiple steps in a changing environment, so diagnosing its failures requires more than inspecting the final response of a large language model (LLM). The same unsuccessful outcome can arise from task difficulty or from an error the agent repeats across tasks. We introduce ProbeAgent, an automated framework that discovers agent failures, tests their proposed causes, and identifies shared failure modes. Starting from benchmark tasks, ProbeAgent builds executable tests and validates them using reference solutions, automated checks, and review of the task requirements. For each failed trajectory, it explains the error and constructs new tasks that preserve the suspected cause while changing the surrounding context. Abstract: According to the reformulated Learned Helplessness theory, repeated exposure to uncontrollable negative events can foster a depressogenic attributional style, increasing susceptibility to depression yet remaining a tractable target for cognitive therapy. Computational research on attributional cognition, however, is hampered by the lack of large-scale datasets and robust evaluation protocols. In this work, we introduce the Attributional Style Transfer Dataset (ASTD) along with dedicated evaluation metrics, the first benchmark designed to model, assess, and reframe attributional explanations at scale. Constructed via a Prevent-Filter-Validate pipeline that integrates LLM-based generation with specialist validation, ASTD contains 42,000 real-world events paired with psychologically grounded attributions spanning seven styles. articles.title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26920v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) develop rich internal representations of language, but whether their individual coordinate axes carry meaning, or whether meaning is encoded only in directions in representation space, is still an open question. A common assumption is that individual axes in LLMs are arbitrary. We here challenge this view: across 12 LLMs from six model families, the native axes are reliably more aligned with other models' representations, with human brain responses to language, and with interpretable linguistic features than randomly rotated axes that preserve the same geometry. The native axes nonetheless fall well short of the best achievable alignment, so LLM coordinates are not fully arbitrary but also not fully canonical: they are partially canonical. articles.title: Beyond Prompt Heuristics: Assessing Child Safety Alignment in LLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26965v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Child-safety taxonomies typically characterize safety risks through a predefined set of harm categories, and existing evaluations largely operationalize these categories using prompts that explicitly invoke them. However, child-safety considerations can also arise in seemingly benign requests that lack recognizable harm-category cues. We therefore investigate how child-safety alignment generalizes to such settings. Across six models, we find considerably higher misalignment rates on requests without recognizable harm-category cues than on those containing such cues (80.0, 54.0, and 48.4 percentage-point gaps for Qwen3.5-27B, GPT-5.4-mini, and Claude-Haiku-4.5, respectively). articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26702v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parameter-efficient prompt learning has become a cornerstone for adapting pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs), yet it remains highly vulnerable to label noise in few-shot Web and retrieval scenarios. Existing noise robust methods typically rely on hard sample selection or deterministic label correction, which discard valuable semantic ambiguity and overlook how observed annotations are actually generated. To bridge this gap, we reformulate noisy prompt learning through the perspective of data generation, proposing SACP, a Semantic-aware Annotation Channel-based Prompt learning framework. Instead of suppressing noise heuristically, SACP decouples latent clean-label prediction from instance-dependent annotation generation. Abstract: Forehead region-of-interest (ROI) localization is important for forehead-creases biometrics, particularly when the lower face is occluded. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26715v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Individual tree segmentation (ITS) from LiDAR point clouds is one of the most widely studied segmentation tasks in forestry. Although deep learning methods define the state of the art on the majority of ITS benchmarks, their high computational complexity and long runtime currently prevent their adoption in large-scale operational workflows. In this work, we present SCATR-ITS, a scalable transformer model specifically designed for efficient ITS over large geographical areas. Based on the ForestFormer3D framework, SCATR-ITS transitions to superpoint-level processing to accelerate inference, with the superpoints constructed from learned embeddings. The architecture incorporates size-aware superpoint-level postprocessing, a dynamic query count module to handle high variation in forest structure, and a maximal input stride designed to minimize prediction redundancy. Abstract: Multi-view learning has shown that combining complementary views can improve predictive performance, yet many datasets provide a single raw source of information. Abstract: Recovering 3D human pose and shape from point clouds is central to motion capture, robotics and self-driving vehicles, because depth cameras and LiDARs sense a person directly in metric 3D and work under any lighting. Abstract: Surgical video analysis requires video object segmentation (VOS), yet existing methods are commonly based on pretrained model fine-tuning using a large number of expert labels. Abstract: We introduce Tracktail, a novel architecture designed to efficiently track query points in 3D from multiple calibrated views without any depth input. Our architecture separates the task as a per-camera video encoding of features and a per-query decoder. Abstract: Whole-body SMPL-X estimators recover body, hand, and face meshes from single images, but applied frame by frame to video they produce jittery motion. Smoothing the output removes the jitter at a cost that body-only benchmarks do not measure: a temporal filter strong enough to steady the torso also flattens the fast finger strokes that carry meaning in sign language and gesture. Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) remain unreliable on spatial reasoning problems that require composing grounded relations across multiple objects. Abstract: Imitation learning for surgical robots is limited by the cost of collecting demonstrations. Meanwhile, many robot-assisted procedures are recorded as stereo video, yet policies cannot learn from them directly; clinical video carries no action labels. We present FlowScope, which pretrains a surgical policy network on unlabeled clinical video by forecasting scene flow, the metric 3D motion of scene points, with labels computed by off-the-shelf stereo depth and optical flow models. Abstract: Learning robotic ultrasound policies requires interactive environments for scalable data generation and repeatable evaluation, while exploration on real patients is limited by acquisition costs and safety constraints. We introduce SonoAtlasWorld, an ultrasound world model built on anatomy as state. A persistent 3D anatomical asset extracted from computed tomography (CT) anchors each scan to a specific anatomy. Probe actions determine anatomical and acoustic visibility conditions for a causal ultrasound generator trained on clinical videos. articles.title: Effectiveness of Synthetic Defects for Anomaly Detection in Industrial Small Load Carriers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26868v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent industrial anomaly detection methods use procedural noise to generate synthetic training defects. Their effectiveness in real-world settings and the impact of different noise generation methods have not been sufficiently investigated. We evaluate the effectiveness of training using synthetic defects for both supervised and unsupervised methods, the impact of different noise generation methods, and the differences in detection performance between benchmark datasets and a real-world small load carrier (SLC) dataset. Trained on synthetic defects only, a supervised classifier reaches 0.65 AUROC on real SLC defects, while three unsupervised methods using the same kind of noise (Perlin) reach 0.87--0.90. Except for SuperSimpleNet, which fails with the foreground-confined fractal Brownian motion (fBm) recipe, models trained with the custom recipe or with nine other noise types do not differ reliably from those trained with Perlin noise.

Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for embodied perception and reasoning, yet their physical understanding is largely evaluated on questions answerable from images. Many properties critical to manipulation, such as an opaque bottle's fill level or an object's compliance, may only be revealed through touch. Four state-of-the-art VLMs average 66.4% accuracy on Tier A relative questions but only 49.8% on Tier B, near chance (50%). articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26902v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An embodied agent cannot afford a large vision-language model (VLM) at every step of a long video, so a cascade runs a small VLM continuously and escalates only uncertain decisions to a large one. Each escalation, however, forces the large model to re-encode a history the small model has already perceived, and this dominates its cost. We present Baton, which hands the large model the small model's visual memory, its key-value (KV) cache over the history. Baton rests on one finding: the large model needs a usable memory, not a faithful copy of its own. A map trained to reproduce the large model's cache matches it most closely, yet brings no gain over the small model alone. Abstract: Zooming into a region often turns a wrong answer from a vision-language model (VLM) into a right one, and a growing literature takes this as evidence that the model lacked the pixels. But a zoom changes several things at once. Abstract: System-level simulation is widely used to validate robotic applications before hardware deployment. Abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26764v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Egocentric videos offer a scalable source of human demonstrations for robot learning. However, recovering metric object geometry and motion from monocular video is hindered by scale-depth ambiguity and hand-induced occlusion, while image-derived contact and shape priors alone cannot uniquely determine metric scale. We introduce TacHOI, a training-free framework that integrates tactile contact with monocular vision for joint hand-object reconstruction and tracking, without requiring object templates or depth sensors. Starting from pretrained visual estimates, TacHOI uses tactile contact to constrain object depth relative to the estimated hand, while spatially separated contacts on a metrically calibrated hand provide a physical ruler for object extent. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26810v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Characterizing user engagement is essential for developing effective human-computer interaction (HCI) applications, particularly for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Because home-based HCI naturally involves caregivers as conversational facilitators, analyzing both child and caregiver vocalizations can provide critical insights into characterizing interaction dynamics. Using a dataset of home-based socially assistive robot (SAR) interventions, this work demonstrates how child and caregiver vocalization patterns can model engagement in HCI contexts. We employed linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) with child and caregiver acoustic data to identify acoustic features that significantly differentiated engagement from disengagement. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26825v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World models based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn from pixels to predict the outcome of actions in a latent space. To reach a goal, a planner samples many candidate action sequences, uses the model to predict where each one leads, and executes the best one. However, standard planners draw their candidates from a Gaussian, while the model has only seen the structured, state-dependent actions of its training data. articles.title: LoCo-WAM: Test-Time Training as Long Context for World-Action Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26853v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World-action models guide robot actions by predicting what happens next, but typically condition on a short observation history. Extending this history increases computation at every decision and can require a separately trained model. We introduce LoCo-WAM, which learns from the outcomes of its actions through test-time training while keeping the same short history length. It uses newly observed frames to update a low-rank adapter in the video expert, whose adapted predictions guide subsequent actions. The updates accumulate within each episode and are reset between episodes, allowing past observations to influence decisions after they leave the input window. LoCo-WAM thus learns from a longer stream of experience without expert action labels, additional data or meta-training. Abstract: Flow matching policies underpin the state-of-the-art in robot learning, with impressive results ranging from long-horizon planning to dexterous manipulation. However, they provide no measure of whether their predicted commands can be trusted, particularly in novel situations outside their training set. Epistemic uncertainty reflects uncertainty about the model's weights and quantifies this ignorance, but calculating it at inference time from a flow matching policy is not trivial. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26858v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models may enable general autonomy in robot planning, but onboard their reasoning can run for most of a minute while the robot and nearby pedestrians keep moving. The robot must then decide how long to follow a plan that the pending answer may overturn. Here we present staleness deadlines, which hand that decision to the robot's clock. Calibrated prediction regions for pedestrians and deviation tubes for the robot set the deadline. Exact binomial tests determine which prespecified budget-selection policies keep close calls, wrong decisions and late arrivals below their targets at each inference profile. articles.title: RoboCap-10k: A Metrically Accurate Egocentric Dataset for Robot Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26916v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Egocentric video is the most scalable source of manipulation data for robot learning, but its difficulty lies in producing high-quality supervision. Existing large corpora lack metric 3D labels or rely on heterogeneous devices, motion-capture labs, or a headset's built-in real-time tracker, whose accuracy is not reported for the released data. We introduce RoboCap-10k: 10,000 curated hours of unscripted manipulation recorded during workers' paid shifts in 11 countries, spanning 18 task families, 200 task types, and 2,000 tasks. Every hour is captured on one device, the RoboCap, a 250 g hat with six synchronized global-shutter cameras and dual IMUs. Online calibration brings every device below 1 px of epipolar error, visual-inertial SLAM yields gravity-aligned 6-DoF head trajectories, and a multi-view hand tracker yields metric cm-precise hand poses. Each episode is annotated with task and sub-task language captions. Project page: https:/

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.26969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Object manipulation in the dynamic real world requires understanding how the environment functions and evolves, and acting accordingly. Existing benchmarks, however, do not adequately address these needs. Physics-oriented benchmarks evaluate predictive fidelity but not closed-loop action. Dynamic robotic manipulation benchmarks often use simplified, physically implausible object motions, limiting evaluation of reasoning and action under realistic dynamics. Evaluation is also typically synchronized, freezing the environment during inference and making computation time irrelevant to task outcomes. To this end, we propose RoboDyna, a benchmark for evaluating the physical understanding and action capabilities of manipulation policies in dynamic scenes. RoboDyna comprises 20 conceptual dynamic tasks spanning five capability categories, with simple objects and minimal scene clutter, under a two-factor difficulty design, and 10 household tasks

Abstract: Robots need contact forces to handle delicate objects, but tactile sensors are fragile and hard to integrate, whereas depth sensors, such as RGB-D cameras, are widely available. articles.content:

Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong performance in grasp-based manipulation, yet reliable recovery from local grasping failures remains challenging. Using force feedback, FoRe partitions demonstrations into approach-grasp and transport-placement stages to train separate policies. Abstract: Simulation-based evaluation of embodied models requires calibrated interactions, diverse tasks, and explicit execution constraints. Abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinating whole-body motion to perform manipulation tasks in complex environments.
